summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, J-tube placement, and Nissen fundoplication was readmitted less than 24 hours after discharge due to recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Symptoms began after increasing her tube feed rate and were consistent with her usual gastroparesis flares. She received IV antiemetics, morphine, and fluids, with resolution of symptoms by the next day. Metabolic acidosis from dehydration improved with treatment, and electrolytes stabilized. She tolerated tube feeds at 90 mL/hr without further vomiting. The gastroenterology team concluded that diagnostic and therapeutic options are exhausted and recommended ongoing symptom management with tube feeds and PRN medications. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged.
